producerFinding.title: Incomplete Prototype Pollution Protection via Blacklist
producerFinding.recommendation: Do not rely on a blacklist checking only '__proto__'. Block or ignore dangerous section identifiers including 'constructor' and 'prototype', or initialize 'out' with Object.create(null) and use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(out, section) to prevent traversing and polluting prototype properties.

ledger.reasoning: The diff adds a check for only `section === '__proto__'`. The following line, `p = out[section] = out[section] || {}`, still runs for other names. Because `out` is a plain object, `out['constructor']` is the inherited `Object` function, which is truthy. So `[constructor]` sets `p` to `Object`, and later key assignments write to global `Object` statics. The blacklist is therefore incomplete, and the hardening recommendation (`Object.create(null)` plus an own-property check) is valid. The locator is accurate: the guard and the assignment are at about lines 12-16 of the new file. The 'high' severity is not shown by the visible diff. `[prototype]` is harmless here, because `out.prototype` is undefined and just creates an own property. Reaching `Object.prototype` would need a nested path such as `constructor.prototype`. The diff shows no dot-splitting of section names, so that path is not visible. The demonstrated impact is tampering with the `Object` function's properties, which is closer to medium. It is not the classic pollution of `Object.prototype`.
